literal: Affliction and sorrow, does he not see, Kama, who abides and acts upon only one person?
translation: Does the god of love, who persists in tormenting only one of us, not see the affliction and sorrow that I suffer?
modern: ஒருவரிடம் மட்டுமே நிலைத்து நின்று செயல்படும் காமன், எனது துன்பத்தையும் வருத்தத்தையும் பார்க்க மாட்டானோ?
explanation: In this couplet, the heroine laments her solitary suffering in separation. She wonders if Kama, the god of love, is blind to her intense distress. She uses the phrase 'oruvaṟkaṇ niṉṟoḻukuvāṉ' (one who abides and acts upon only one person) to point out the unfairness of her situation. Love should affect both partners equally, yet she feels that Kama has targeted only her, leaving her to bear the twin burdens of affliction ('paruvaral') and sorrow ('paital') alone.
